Canva AI turns a description into an editable design: a post, a deck, a website, a video or a doc.
Free accounts get up to 20 Premium AI uses a month, Pro gets up to 200, and you can check what is left under Settings, then Billing.

slides.headline: How to use *Canva AI*: designs, slides and what each plan gets

slides.heading: 1. Describe the *whole design*
paras: Tell Canva AI the format, the goal and the audience. It builds a full design you can edit.
It works for social posts, presentations, websites, videos and docs.

slides.heading: 2. Plug in your *Brand Kit*
paras: With a Brand Kit connected, Canva AI uses your colors, fonts and tone.
Tag @Canva in a comment to get design feedback without writing a long prompt.

slides.heading: 3. Fix *one thing* at a time
paras: Ask for one change, like a new headline or image. Canva says the rest of the design stays put.
Style Match pulls a messy design together. Magic Background makes a backdrop that fits.

slides.heading: 4. Watch your *AI allowance*
paras: Free: up to 20 Premium AI uses a month. Pro: up to 200, plus 20 Ultra.
Chat-style design uses more per request. Check it under Settings, then Billing.

site_article.headline: How to use Canva AI: designs, presentations and what each plan gets
site_article.dek: What Canva AI can build from one description, the steps that get a usable first draft, and how the monthly AI allowance works on each plan.
site_article.summary: Canva AI turns a written description into a complete, editable design and can generate single elements, presentations and feedback. This guide walks through the steps and explains the monthly AI allowance, from up to 20 Premium uses on Canva Free to up to 400 on Business.
site_article.seo_title: How to use Canva AI: designs, slides and limits by plan
site_article.seo_description: How to use Canva AI step by step: describe a design, build a presentation, use your Brand Kit, three prompts to copy, and the AI limits on each plan.
site_article.answer_summary: Describe the design you need to Canva AI, including the format, goal and audience, and it generates a complete design you can edit piece by piece. Every plan has a monthly AI allowance, which you can check by selecting your profile icon, then Settings, then Billing.
site_article.hero_alt: Promotional image from Canva showing its AI design tools.

paragraphs.text: How to use Canva AI comes down to three habits: describe the whole design instead of one picture, edit the result one element at a time, and keep an eye on your monthly AI allowance. Canva AI is the assistant built into Canva. You describe what you need in a chat, and it generates a design you can keep editing, according to Engadget and 9to5Mac's coverage of the Canva AI 2.0 launch in April 2026.

Canva says its own Canva Design Model now powers these features. The company describes it as a model trained on design structure, layering, hierarchy and branding, and says it creates fully editable content rather than a flat image. The same model is also available inside ChatGPT and Claude, Canva says.
What Canva AI can make

According to Canva's newsroom, the main pieces are: AI-powered designs (a complete design for a social post, presentation, website, video or doc), AI-powered elements (photos, videos, icons, shapes, 3D elements and custom code from the Elements tab), Style Match (makes the look of a design consistent), Magic Background (a backdrop that fits the subject, layout and style), Guided Presentations, Magic Video and Ask @Canva, which gives feedback when you tag it in a comment.

Two newer models sit on top of that. Canva Craft, Canva's first image generation model, launched on October 22, 2026 in the Dream Lab tab and outputs images up to 2K, Tech Insider reported. Canva Brush, launched October 29, works through a design step by step and was available only to Canva Pro subscribers at launch, according to Fast Company.
How to use Canva AI, step by step

paragraphs.title: 1. Start from the Canva AI chat
paragraphs.text: Canva AI 2.0 is a conversational interface: you type what you need and it creates, edits and organizes the work. It launched as a research preview starting from the Canva homepage, with access widening over time, so the exact entry point can differ by account.

paragraphs.title: 2. Describe the whole design, not one image
paragraphs.text: Say the format, the goal, the audience and the tone in one message. Canva AI is built to generate a complete design with structure and layout, so a full brief gets you a usable first draft instead of a random picture.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: A social post from a brief
paragraphs.text: Make an Instagram carousel of 5 slides announcing [event] on [date] at [place]. Audience: [who]. Tone: friendly and clear. Put the date and place on the first slide and a call to sign up on the last.

paragraphs.title: 3. For a deck, use Guided Presentations
paragraphs.text: Canva says Guided Presentations is a conversational flow on the Canva AI homepage that first asks about your goal, then helps shape the story and structure the slides before you pick a layout. Answer its questions properly: the outline you agree on decides how good the slides are.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: A presentation outline
paragraphs.text: I need a 10 slide presentation for [audience] about [topic]. The goal is to get them to [decision or action]. Use one idea per slide, end with a slide of next steps, and keep text under 25 words per slide.

paragraphs.title: 4. Connect your Brand Kit
paragraphs.text: Once a Brand Kit is connected, Canva AI generates designs that reflect the brand's colors, fonts, tone and style, according to Canva. Engadget also reported a brand tool that applies a company's visual identity to new and existing designs. Do this before you generate, not after.

paragraphs.title: 5. Change one element at a time
paragraphs.text: Canva AI 2.0 edits only the element you name, such as an image, a headline or a font, 9to5Mac reported. Ask for small, specific changes. If the parts of a design look mismatched, try Style Match; if the background looks empty, try Magic Background.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: A targeted fix
paragraphs.text: Keep everything else the same. Replace the headline on slide 1 with a shorter one under 8 words, and make the photo on slide 3 warmer and brighter.

paragraphs.title: 6. Ask @Canva for feedback
paragraphs.text: Tag @Canva in a comment on your design. Canva says it gives design feedback and can generate visuals, using fonts, colors and tone that fit, without extra prompts.
Canva AI limits on each plan

Every plan has one monthly AI allowance shared by Standard, Premium and Ultra tools, and Premium and Ultra tools use more of it per use. On Canva Free and Pro Lite, Standard tools count toward the allowance, with up to 20 Premium uses shared with Standard, and no Ultra tools. Canva Pro, Teams and Nonprofits get up to 200 Premium uses and up to 20 Ultra uses, and Standard tools such as Magic Write and Translate do not count. Business and Enterprise get up to 400 Premium and up to 40 Ultra uses.

The numbers are a best case. Canva says they assume simple prompts and the cheapest tool in each category, and that Canva AI 2.0 conversational design uses more than single prompt features, rising with the size of the design, the complexity of the task and the model needed. Designs made through ChatGPT or Claude connected to Canva also draw from your allowance.

To see what is left, select your profile icon, then Settings, then Billing, and look under AI usage. Free allowances reset at midnight UTC on the first of each month; paid plans reset on the billing date.

When you run out on Free, Canva adds short pauses between Standard and Premium generations and blocks Ultra tools until the reset. You can upgrade, buy an AI Pass or a top-up where your plan allows it, or wait.
Where Canva AI falls short

The allowance is the real limit. Chat-style editing is the most useful part of Canva AI and also the most expensive per request, so a long back and forth on a big deck can use far more of a Free month than the headline number suggests. Some of the newest tools, like Brush, started on paid plans only, and the AI 2.0 assistant rolled out gradually, so not every account sees the same features at the same time. Treat the first draft as a layout to edit, check every fact and number in it yourself, and spend your AI uses on the changes that would take longest by hand.
